title: Best Dehumidifier for Sunroom (2026): Heated & Unheated
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for a Sunroom
dek: A room made of glass follows the weather. Pick a dehumidifier that can keep up when the sun goes down and the windows start to sweat.
description: The best dehumidifier for a sunroom in 2026 — compressor picks for heated four-season rooms and cold-proof desiccant units for unheated three-season ones.
intro: Finding the best **dehumidifier for a sunroom** comes down to one question: is the room heated? A sunroom is mostly glass, and single-pane glass insulates at roughly **R-1**, versus R-13 to R-21 for a typical insulated wall, according to the U.S. Department of Energy. So a sunroom tracks the outdoor temperature far more closely than any other room in the house.

That has two consequences. On cool mornings, warm indoor air hits cold glass and condenses into streams of water that pool on sills and frames. And in an unheated three-season room, nights can drop below the temperature where an ordinary compressor dehumidifier can even work — just when the glass is producing the most condensation.
So we split our picks by room type: compressor units for heated four-season sunrooms, and a desiccant model that keeps going in the cold.
topPicksLead: For a heated, four-season sunroom, the **Midea Cube 50** is the best overall pick — quiet, efficient and Wi-Fi-connected so you can catch rising humidity before the glass fogs.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for sunrooms

blocks.text: We don’t lab-test. We compared published operating temperature ranges, capacity ratings (DOE where available, AHAM for commercial units), coverage and drainage options from manuals and spec sheets, and read owner reviews for cold-weather icing, noise in living spaces and condensation control.
Because the heated-versus-unheated question decides more than capacity does, we chose at least one strong pick for each type of room, plus a large-room and a budget option.

sections.heading: What to look for in a sunroom dehumidifier

items.label: A type that matches your heat
items.text: Heated four-season room: any good compressor unit. Unheated three-season room: a desiccant that works near freezing.

items.label: Capacity sized to the glass
items.text: Lots of glass means more condensation per square foot than an ordinary room. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) helps you size up.

items.label: Drainage that suits the room
items.text: Most sunrooms have no floor drain. A pump or a hose out to the yard keeps the unit running unattended.

items.label: Quiet operation
items.text: A sunroom is often a reading or relaxing room, so check owner comments about noise.

items.label: A hygrometer near the glass
items.text: Cold glass can fog even at humidity that’s fine elsewhere. Watch the reading, not just the feel of the air.

sections.heading: Heated vs. unheated sunrooms: which dehumidifier?

blocks.text: If you’re not sure how cold the room gets, leave a thermometer-hygrometer in it for a week in late fall. If the overnight lows dip near 40°F, choose desiccant.

sections.heading: How to stop sunroom window condensation

items: Keep relative humidity around 30–50%, toward the low end in cold weather.
Run the dehumidifier overnight and in the early morning, when glass is coldest.
Keep air moving with a ceiling fan so moist air doesn’t stall against the glass.
Move plants away from the windows, or reduce how many you water heavily in winter.
Close the door between the sunroom and the house on cold nights if the room is unheated, so warm, moist indoor air doesn’t flow in and condense.
Wipe sills and frames dry each morning until humidity is under control.

blocks.text: Condensation on house windows more generally? See our guide to using a [dehumidifier for condensation on windows](/guides/dehumidifier-for-condensation-on-windows/).

sections.heading: Where to put a dehumidifier in a sunroom

blocks.text: Placement matters more in a glass room than almost anywhere else, because the problem is concentrated on the coldest surfaces.

items: **Near the worst windows, not against them.** Two to three feet from the glass lets the unit catch moist air as it drifts toward the cold panes without blocking its own airflow.
**Out of direct afternoon sun.** Baking in a sunbeam makes a compressor work harder and can fool its humidity sensor.
**Close to a drain path.** A hose out a door or to a floor drain saves daily bucket trips in humid months.
**On a mat or tray.** Sunroom floors are often tile or wood; a tray catches drips during bucket changes.

blocks.text: For general rules that apply in any room, see [where to place a dehumidifier](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/).

For a heated, four-season sunroom, the **Midea Cube 50** is the best all-around choice. For an unheated three-season room, skip compressor models and go with the **Ivation 13-Pint Desiccant**, which keeps working down to 33°F. Choose the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S** for a large, glass-heavy space and the **Frigidaire FFAD2233W1** only for a small or warm-season room. If your sunroom doubles as a plant room, read our [best dehumidifier for plants](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-plants/) guide first — most houseplants want more humidity than you might think.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for a sunroom?
faqs.a: For a heated sunroom, the Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT). For an unheated three-season sunroom, the Ivation 13-Pint Desiccant, which keeps working down to 33°F.

faqs.q: Why do sunroom windows get so much condensation?
faqs.a: Glass insulates poorly, so it gets much colder than the room air. When warm, moist air touches cold glass, it drops below its dew point and condenses. Lowering humidity and moving air reduces it.

faqs.q: Will a regular dehumidifier work in an unheated sunroom?
faqs.a: Not reliably in cold weather. Compressor units start icing below about 41°F and stop removing meaningful moisture. A desiccant dehumidifier is the better choice for three-season rooms.

faqs.q: What humidity should a sunroom be?
faqs.a: About 30–50% relative humidity. In cold weather, aim for the lower end, because the glass can fog even when the rest of the room feels comfortable.

faqs.q: Can I use a small dehumidifier in a sunroom?
faqs.a: Yes, for a small sunroom under about 300 square feet used mainly in warm months. A budget unit like the Frigidaire FFAD2233W1 works well there, but it will struggle once the room gets cold.

faqs.q: Where should I put a dehumidifier in a sunroom?
faqs.a: Two to three feet from the windows that fog most, out of direct sun, with at least a foot of clearance on all sides and a short path to a drain or door for the hose.
